intro.title: Clone Graph
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that creates a deep copy, or clone, of a graph data structure. You will learn how to traverse a graph using breadth-first search (BFS) to visit all nodes and their neighbors. The main technologies involved are JavaScript objects, arrays, and queues to manage the traversal process. By the end, you will understand how to handle complex data structures and avoid reference issues when copying them.
intro.usecase: The Clone Graph algorithm is essential in applications that need to duplicate complex interconnected data structures, such as social networks where you need to copy a user's entire friend network for analysis or backup. In collaborative tools like Figma or Miro, when you duplicate a complex diagram with multiple connected elements, the system must replicate all nodes and their relationships accurately. This pattern also appears in version control systems when branching repositories, and in game development when cloning entire scene graphs with their object hierarchies and dependencies.
